user.title: Connect an ISAPI camera
user.description: Use the camera's local ISAPI credentials. Set HTTP/HTTPS and its matching port explicitly. One entry monitors one camera channel. Enable camera event detection and Notify Surveillance Center in the camera UI.

data_description.host: Local camera IP or hostname, without a URL, port or path.
data_description.username: A camera account allowed to read ISAPI settings and receive events.
data_description.password: Your camera password. It is saved in Home Assistant's config entry and never filled back into this form. On reconfigure or reauthentication, leave blank to keep it.
data_description.port: HTTP or HTTPS port configured on the camera (usually 80 or 443).
data_description.use_ssl: Use HTTPS for encrypted camera traffic; set the matching HTTPS port.
data_description.verify_ssl: Validate the HTTPS certificate, including the hostname/IP match. Self-signed or mismatched camera certificates may require disabling this; traffic stays encrypted but camera identity is not verified.
data_description.channel: Video input number, usually 1 for a standalone camera. This selects the input to monitor; it does not change camera settings or select main/substream.

reconfigure.title: Edit camera connection
reconfigure.description: Leave the password blank to keep the saved password. This must be the same camera and channel.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot read ISAPI device information. Check the address, port, camera access settings, and certificate.
error.invalid_auth: The camera rejected the credentials or device information permission.
error.invalid_host: Enter only a hostname or IP address, without a URL, port, or path.
error.wrong_device: This address or channel belongs to a different camera. Add it as a separate entry.
error.unknown: Unexpected connection error. Check the Home Assistant log for the generic error category and try again.
error.invalid_certificate: The camera's HTTPS certificate could not be verified. Use a trusted certificate matching its hostname, or disable Verify HTTPS certificate if the camera's identity has been verified separately.

abort.already_configured: This camera channel is already configured.

init.title: Camera monitoring options
init.description: Detections turn on immediately. After a trigger ends, the off debounce keeps the sensor on for the configured delay. A new trigger cancels the pending off transition. Camera health/availability is not debounced.

data_description.alarm_hold: Fallback when the camera never sends an inactive event: infer the end after this many seconds without an active update, then apply the off debounce. Set 0 to wait for an explicit inactive event.
data_description.debounce_seconds: Keep detection sensors HIGH for this many seconds after the last trigger ends. New activity cancels the pending LOW transition. 0 clears immediately. Applies to detected alarms, not connection diagnostics.
data_description.parameter_entities: Create disabled diagnostic entities for readable camera parameters. Enable individual entities as needed.

error.invalid_options: Enter a timeout and debounce between 0 and 3600 seconds.
